summary: The Relevance Gate is told what it is looking at — which end of the transcript is new, how old each line is, and what her standing note means.
details: Every transcript line now carries how long ago it was sent. Three of the gate's judgements are about time — has the room moved past this, is it still waiting, did somebody already answer — and it was making all three on a wall of undated lines. Nora's own turns have had this since they were built.
The gate is now told the transcript is oldest-first, so 'judge the recent lines' has a direction. It was never stated.

Her standing note arrives explained: what it is, that it is the only thing that can establish something she owes the room, and that an empty one means she has not written one rather than that she owes nothing.

Measured over the suite's 40 labelled windows: false NO_GO fell from a median of 3 to 1 across six runs, with one run at zero and every capability full. No false GO, safety 6/6 throughout, and about 170 extra prompt tokens.
limitations: The eval fixture had to gain real timestamps to measure this — it had been dating every case to 1970, which no renderer had read until now.
Run-to-run variation is real: the same 40 cases score between 0 and 2 on this build. The improvement is in the distribution, not in any single run.
